questions.learningObjective: Match an advertisement to its target audience
questions.stem: In a workplace report, explain how an advertisement's vocabulary and imagery reveal the target audience it seeks to reach.

answer.exemplar: The advertisement's vocabulary and imagery signal its target audience by choosing references, registers, and situations that the intended readers already recognise and value, while excluding others.

questions.explanation: Vocabulary and imagery work as audience filters by matching shared references. A mismatched register signals a different group, which is why the same product can be pitched differently.

options.text: To make the cause harder to identify
To remove the date from the story
To direct reader sympathy and attention
To shorten the headline to one word

questions.explanation: Foregrounding the victim directs sympathy and attention. It does not conceal the cause, delete dates, or shorten the headline.
questions.hint: Ask what attention the choice buys.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how an advertisement signals its audience
questions.stem: In a workplace report, explain how an advertisement signals its target audience through setting.

options.text: The main claim itself

The author's name
The condition that limited the claim

options.text: A vague thanks to the brand hidden in the comments
options.misconception: treats a hidden thanks as adequate

options.text: A wink emoji with no words
A clear paid-partnership label placed with the post
A link to the brand with no label
options.misconception: confuses a link with a label

questions.explanation: A clear paid-partnership label with the post is adequate. Hidden thanks, emojis, and bare links are not.

answer.exemplar: A verified fact has been checked by the reporter, while an attributed statement is reported as someone's claim and may still be unverified.

options.text: Whether the speaker intended to deceive
Whether the claim matched the original source
options.misconception: confuses the checked item with the unchecked one

Whether the claim used a date

questions.learningObjective: Identify a signal a feed ignores

options.text: Whether the user actually read the item
The number of clicks the item received
options.misconception: confuses the optimised signal with the overlooked one

options.text: The date the item was published
The author's name

questions.explanation: A click-optimised feed overlooks whether the user read the item. Clicks are its signal, and date and author are separate.

Turning off the device entirely

Turning off all cameras
Speakers pause briefly before replying
